about.h1: One clear view of your kitchen operations.
about.intro: KitchFlow is a kitchen operations management app for restaurants and cafés that combines inventory management, food-waste tracking, staff scheduling, task management and supplier management.
about.togetherTitle: Five essential workflows. One kitchen app.
about.togetherBody: KitchFlow is a kitchen operations management app for restaurants and cafés that combines inventory management, food-waste tracking, staff scheduling, task management and supplier management.
about.serviceBody: Keep daily work visible to the whole team instead of scattered across notebooks, spreadsheets and chat threads.
about.whoTitle: Made for teams close to the work.
about.whoBody: KitchFlow is designed for café owners, restaurant managers, kitchen leads and small food-service teams who need one shared operational picture.
about.availableBody: Download the app from the App Store and bring inventory, waste, staff, tasks and suppliers into one workflow. Android is not available yet.

inventory.definition: KitchFlow inventory management helps kitchens count stock, set reorder points, receive deliveries with QR scanning and turn low stock into shopping lists.
inventory.problemBody: Running out mid-service costs covers. Over-ordering ties up cash and fills the walk-in with product that spoils. Spreadsheets work until multiple people update them at once.

features.title: Counts and par levels
features.body: Record on-hand quantities and reorder points so the team knows what to order before service.

features.title: QR receiving
features.body: Scan deliveries to update stock faster than typing every line by hand.

features.title: Shopping lists from stock
features.body: Build supplier lists from items under par instead of guessing from memory.

inventory.whoBody: Cafe owners, restaurant managers and kitchen leads who need inventory visible to the whole team, not locked in one person's notebook.

faqs.q: What does KitchFlow inventory management do?
faqs.a: It tracks on-hand stock, reorder points, receiving and shopping lists inside the KitchFlow kitchen ops app.

faqs.q: Is it suitable for small cafés?
faqs.a: Yes. Small cafés can start with the highest-cost items and expand as the menu grows.

inventory.relatedBlog: How to start a small cafe: inventory guide

waste.definition: KitchFlow food waste tracking lets teams log discards by reason, see cost impact and fix the ordering or prep issues that create waste.
waste.problemBody: Waste often leaves a little at a time: unsold pastry, over-steamed milk, prep mistakes. Without a log, owners guess instead of fixing the biggest sources.

features.title: Reason tags
features.body: Tag spoilage, prep error, overproduction or returns so patterns show up quickly.

features.title: Cost attached
features.body: Connect waste entries to cost so the team sees margin impact, not only volume.

features.title: Cafe-specific habits
features.body: Works for pastry cases, dairy and espresso bars, not only full restaurant kitchens.

waste.whoBody: Restaurants and cafés that already run inventory but still lose margin to silent waste.

faqs.a: Yes. Log waste by reason with cost attached and review trends inside KitchFlow.

faqs.q: Do I need software on day one?
faqs.a: A paper or spreadsheet log works at first. Move to KitchFlow when volume makes manual entry slip.

staff.definition: KitchFlow staff scheduling helps managers invite team members, publish shifts and keep ownership clear across service periods.
staff.problemBody: Double-booked shifts and no-shows usually come from chat threads and informal swaps, not from bad people. The schedule needs one source of truth.

features.title: Invite by code
features.body: Add staff without long onboarding flows so the roster stays current.

features.title: Shift visibility
features.body: Publish who is on when so prep and service coverage are obvious.

features.title: Tied to kitchen ops
features.body: Scheduling sits next to tasks and inventory, not in a separate disconnected tool.

staff.whoBody: Managers running multi-person cafe or restaurant teams who need coverage without another spreadsheet.

faqs.a: Yes. Invite staff, manage shifts and keep the roster inside the same kitchen ops app.

tasks.definition: KitchFlow kitchen task management turns opening, closing and prep work into owned checklists with clear accountability.
tasks.problemTitle: When tasks live in someone's head
tasks.problemBody: If only one lead knows the opening list, quality drops when that person is off. Written tasks with owners fix that.

features.title: Opening and closing lists
features.body: Standardize shift routines so the same work happens every day.

features.title: Named ownership
features.body: Attach a person to each task so nothing sits as 'someone will do it'.

features.title: Activity visibility
features.body: See what was completed when, next to inventory and waste logs.

tasks.whoBody: Kitchens that need consistent prep and cleaning standards across rotating staff.

faqs.a: Yes. Managers can assign checklists and track completion inside KitchFlow.

supplier.definition: KitchFlow supplier tools help kitchens turn under-par inventory into shopping lists instead of ordering from memory.
supplier.problemBody: When ordering is disconnected from counts, teams buy what feels right. That creates overstock on slow movers and stockouts on busy items.

features.title: Lists from inventory
features.body: Generate shopping needs from items under reorder points.

features.title: Fewer forgotten lines
features.body: Keep milk, cups and dry goods on the same operational list the team already uses.

features.title: One ops workflow
features.body: Ordering sits beside receiving, waste and tasks in KitchFlow.

supplier.whoBody: Operators who already count stock and want purchasing to follow those numbers.

faqs.a: Yes. Shopping lists can be built from inventory levels so orders match real needs.
